title: Shorter paths had later response centroids in passive models of two partial adult worm electrical maps
abstract: We tested whether fewer wiring steps give an earlier response centroid in passive models of two partial adult C. elegans electrical maps. At uniform leak 0.1, the shorter-hop destination had a centroid at least 1 percent later in 12195 of 508533 eligible comparisons in map 7 (2.40 percent), and 17277 of 651797 in map 8 (2.65 percent). Both destinations had normalized steady transfer at least 0.01. Equal link weights reduced these shares to 1.01 and 1.67 percent. Leak and response selection changed the shares. A four-cell tree gave a separate example. Matrix integrals, independent eigen calculations and numerical quadrature checked the method. Partial annotations, assumed conductance and cell parameters, and no matched activity limit the result to these models. Original code, aggregate evidence, source hashes and external retrieval steps support reproduction. External records and graph matrices are not bundled.

display.caption: Shorter-hop destinations can have later response centroids. Fractions depend on leak, weight assumptions and response selection. At leak 10 there are no eligible unequal-hop comparisons at the primary response floor.
